sections.content:
You know *con miras a* and *con vistas a* ("with a view to") from B2 Unit 12 and *con el fin de* ("in order to") from B1 Unit 32. All three look ahead to a goal. This lesson adds two phrases that weigh a goal against what it costs:

• *en aras de*: "for the sake of". It names a value that someone gives something up for: *en aras de la paz*, *en aras del equipo*. What follows is something good.
• *a costa de*: "at the expense of". It names what is lost or harmed to get something: *a costa de su salud*, *a costa de dormir poco*.

Both take a noun, and both can take an infinitive. Remember *de* + *el* becomes *del*. So the three ideas are: *con miras a* is the goal, *en aras de* is the value you serve, and *a costa de* is the price you pay.

sections.title: The goal, the value and the price
rows: Amplían la oficina con miras a contratar más personal.
They are enlarging the office with a view to hiring more staff.
Las dos partes cedieron en aras de la paz.
Both sides gave way for the sake of peace.
Esa empresa gana dinero a costa del medio ambiente.
That company makes money at the expense of the environment.

sections.content: *En aras de* sounds positive: the aim is something valued, like peace or the team. For what you lose, use *a costa de*. Do not use *en aras de* for something bad: you cannot give something up *en aras de* a problem.
